metadata.title: QA Persona Testing - Sources
metadata.description: Primary references for persona-based / synthetic-user app testing: LLM persona simulation research, validity critiques, severity models, web-agent task design, and browser automation tooling.

persona_simulation_research.name: UXAgent: An LLM-Agent-Based Usability Testing Framework (system paper)
persona_simulation_research.description: Reference architecture: Persona Generator + LLM Agent Module (with memory/interaction log) + Universal Browser Connector + Result Viewer for simulated usability testing.

persona_simulation_research.name: UXAgent CHI'25 extended abstract
persona_simulation_research.description: Earlier UXAgent write-up; heuristic evaluation with UX researchers and practitioner concerns about LLM-agent usability studies.

persona_simulation_research.name: Persona2Web: Benchmarking Personalized Web Agents
persona_simulation_research.description: Personalization from implicit user preference history rather than explicit instructions; basis for persona memory/state design.

persona_simulation_research.name: The Chameleon's Limit: Persona Fidelity and Population Homogenization in LLMs
persona_simulation_research.description: 10 models, 1,144 personas, 26 identity dimensions. Source of the fidelity trap (every model at fidelity rho > 0.9 also showed between-group Cohen's d > 6) and the attribute-truncation mention rates (gender 89%, country 86%, ideology 60%, age 33%, social class 25%). Figures verified against the arXiv HTML full text, not a secondary summary.

persona_simulation_research.name: Occupational persona audit against US BLS demographics
persona_simulation_research.description: 1.5M+ generated occupational personas compared with BLS data across 41 occupations; demographic skew recurs across models with unrelated training origins, making it structural rather than vendor-specific. Grounds the confidence downgrade for specialist/enterprise personas.

persona_simulation_research.name: Simulating Identity: persona prompting does not reduce stereotyping
persona_simulation_research.description: Persona conditioning changed surface wording without reducing abstraction/stereotyping bias; in-group personas stereotyped as much as out-group ones. Grounds the rule that a persona label is not a bias control.

validity_and_limits.name: NN/g: Evaluating AI-Simulated Behavior — Three Studies on Digital Twins and Synthetic Users
validity_and_limits.description: Synthesis of 2024-2025 studies: lower variance, direction-over-magnitude reliability, interview-grounded twins (85%) vs demographic-only (55%), ethical-disclosure guidance.

validity_and_limits.name: The Illusion of Intervention: Your LLM-Simulated Experiment is an Observational Study
validity_and_limits.description: Methodological argument that persona-conditioned simulation is observational, not interventional; grounds the no-causal-claims rule.

validity_and_limits.name: Catching UX Flaws in Code: Leveraging LLMs to Identify Usability Flaws (IEEE VL/HCC 2025)
validity_and_limits.description: Empirical reliability data: moderate issue-detection agreement (Kappa ~0.50) but weak severity-rating reliability (near-zero Krippendorff's Alpha); grounds the second-pass severity rule.

validity_and_limits.name: Intersectional Sycophancy in Multi-Turn LLM Conversations
validity_and_limits.description: 768 multi-turn conversations x 128 personas x 3 domains. Primary source for the anti-sycophancy rules: model choice dominates (GPT-5-nano 2.96 vs Claude Haiku 4.5 1.74, p < 1e-32), subjective domains elicit ~41% more sycophancy than mathematics, and the effect is intersectional rather than tied to one demographic axis. Grounds the 'record the model' session-log field and the mandatory adversarial pass on subjective surfaces.

validity_and_limits.name: Synthetic users vs real participants (practitioner critique)
validity_and_limits.description: Practitioner color on sycophancy and identity flattening. Demoted 2026-08-01: no longer load-bearing now that arXiv:2604.11609 and arXiv:2604.24698 cover the same failure modes with primary data. Keep only as corroboration.

methods_and_scales.name: NN/g: How to Rate the Severity of Usability Problems
methods_and_scales.description: Canonical 0-4 severity scale used by the session log and findings report.

methods_and_scales.name: NN/g: Thinking Aloud — The #1 Usability Tool
methods_and_scales.description: Think-aloud protocol conventions mirrored by the dual-channel session log.

web_agent_task_design.name: WebArena benchmark
web_agent_task_design.description: Reproducible, bounded, verifiable web-task design pattern used for scenario construction.

tooling.name: Playwright MCP
tooling.description: Official Playwright MCP server: accessibility-tree snapshots and browser tools used in Phase 3. Verify tool names here before prescribing calls.

tooling.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
tooling.description: Chrome DevTools MCP server: console, network, performance, and emulation evidence channels. Source for the emulate parameter set (viewport with mobile/touch flags, networkConditions, cpuThrottlingRate, geolocation, colorScheme) and for isolatedContext page isolation.

tooling.name: Playwright CLI
tooling.description: Official shell-based companion to Playwright MCP: snapshots are written to disk as compact YAML with element refs rather than returned inline, so token cost stays flat across long runs. Positioned for token-constrained coding-agent work; this skill uses it for regression re-checks, not exploratory persona discovery. Token-reduction figures circulating in practitioner blogs are secondary — do not cite a magnitude.
